input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 grants unlimited, unannounced audits plus remote access to our systems and records — walk-away territory on frequency, notice and system access, and it fails the fallback (once a year on 15 days' notice, no system access). Sections 22.2 and 22.3 are acceptable (Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access, findings are our Confidential Information) but directly conflict with 22.1, so we rewrote 22.1 to the preferred position: once per twelve months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, off-site where practicable, and no remote or direct system access.

proposal.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor, no system access
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the unlimited, unannounced audit right and remote access to our systems with a once-per-twelve-months audit on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, which also removes the conflict with Section 22.2. We can accept 15 days' notice as a fallback, but direct or remote access to our systems is not available.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours, and only through an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations. Each audit will be conducted off-site wherever practicable and limited to records relevant to Customer's usage; neither Vendor nor its auditor may access Customer's systems remotely or otherwise.
